Acne vulgaris is a common skin condition characterized by the presence of comedones, papules, pustules, and sometimes nodules or cysts, typically affecting areas with a high density of sebaceous glands such as the face, chest, and back. 2. Acne rosacea, or simply rosacea, is a chronic inflammatory skin condition primarily affecting the central face, presenting with erythema, telangiectasia, papules, and pustules, often triggered by environmental or dietary factors. 3. Cutaneous anthrax is a bacterial infection caused by Bacillus anthracis, presenting as a painless ulcer with a characteristic black eschar, often accompanied by significant surrounding edema. 4. Bacillary angiomatosis is a vascular proliferative disease caused by Bartonella species, typically seen in immunocompromised individuals, presenting as red to purple papules or nodules that may ulcerate. 5. Bite wounds, whether from animals or humans, carry a high risk of infection due to the introduction of oral flora into the wound, necessitating careful cleaning and often prophylactic antibiotics. 6. Bubonic plague, caused by Yersinia pestis, is characterized by the sudden onset of fever, chills, and painful lymphadenopathy (buboes), often associated with a history of flea exposure or contact with infected animals. 7. A carbuncle is a deep, multiloculated abscess involving multiple hair follicles, typically caused by Staphylococcus aureus, and often requires incision and drainage in addition to antibiotic therapy. 8. Cat scratch disease, caused by Bartonella henselae, presents with regional lymphadenopathy following a scratch or bite from a cat, often accompanied by fever and malaise. 9. Cellulitis is a bacterial infection of the dermis and subcutaneous tissue, presenting with erythema, warmth, swelling, and tenderness, most commonly caused by Streptococcus or Staphylococcus species. 10. Ecthyma is a deeper form of impetigo that extends into the dermis, presenting as ulcerative lesions with a thick crust, often caused by Streptococcus pyogenes or Staphylococcus aureus. 11. Erysipelas is a superficial bacterial skin infection involving the upper dermis and lymphatics, presenting with well-demarcated erythema, warmth, and swelling, most commonly caused by Streptococcus pyogenes. 12. Erysipeloid is a localized skin infection caused by Erysipelothrix rhusiopathiae, typically seen in individuals handling raw fish or meat, presenting as a painful, violaceous lesion on the hands or fingers. 13. Erythrasma is a superficial bacterial infection caused by Corynebacterium minutissimum, presenting as well-demarcated, reddish-brown patches in intertriginous areas, often fluorescing coral-red under Wood's lamp. 14. Fournier gangrene is a rapidly progressive necrotizing fasciitis of the perineum and genitalia, often polymicrobial in origin, requiring emergent surgical debridement and broad-spectrum antibiotics. 15. A furuncle, or boil, is a deep folliculitis caused by Staphylococcus aureus, presenting as a painful, erythematous nodule with purulent drainage. 16. Gas gangrene, or clostridial myonecrosis, is a life-threatening infection caused by Clostridium species, characterized by rapid tissue necrosis, gas production, and systemic toxicity. 17. Glanders, caused by Burkholderia mallei, is a rare zoonotic infection presenting with cutaneous ulcers, lymphadenopathy, and systemic symptoms, often associated with contact with infected equines. 18. Impetigo is a superficial bacterial skin infection, commonly caused by Staphylococcus aureus or Streptococcus pyogenes, presenting as honey-colored crusted lesions, with bullous and non-bullous forms. 19. Lyme disease with cutaneous manifestations, such as erythema migrans, is caused by Borrelia burgdorferi and transmitted via tick bites, often accompanied by systemic symptoms. 20. Mastitis is an infection of the breast tissue, commonly occurring during lactation, presenting with localized pain, erythema, and systemic symptoms such as fever, often caused by Staphylococcus aureus. 21. Necrotizing fasciitis is a severe, rapidly progressive infection of the fascia and subcutaneous tissue, often polymicrobial or caused by Group A Streptococcus, requiring emergent surgical intervention. 22. A pilonidal cyst is a chronic infection of the skin and subcutaneous tissue near the coccyx, often presenting with pain, swelling, and purulent drainage. 23. Pyomyositis is a bacterial infection of skeletal muscle, often caused by Staphylococcus aureus, presenting with localized pain, swelling, and systemic symptoms such as fever. 24. Seborrheic dermatitis is a chronic inflammatory skin condition affecting sebaceous gland-rich areas, presenting with erythematous, scaly patches, often associated with Malassezia species. 25. Skin and soft tissue infections in neutropenic fever require prompt evaluation and empiric broad-spectrum antibiotics due to the high risk of invasive bacterial or fungal infections. 26. Skin and soft tissue infections in cellular immunodeficiency are often caused by opportunistic pathogens, requiring tailored antimicrobial therapy based on the underlying immune defect. 27. Surgical site infections occur at or near the surgical incision site, presenting with erythema, swelling, and purulent drainage, often caused by Staphylococcus aureus or other skin flora. 28. Tularemia, caused by Francisella tularensis, is a zoonotic infection presenting with ulceroglandular, glandular, or other forms, often associated with exposure to infected animals or arthropod vectors. 29. Vascular insufficiency ulcers, such as venous or arterial ulcers, are chronic wounds resulting from impaired blood flow, often complicated by secondary infection. 30. Vibrio infections, caused by Vibrio species, are often associated with exposure to seawater or raw seafood, presenting with cellulitis, necrotizing fasciitis, or septicemia. 31. Wound infections occur when bacteria colonize a wound, leading to erythema, swelling, pain, and purulent drainage, often requiring debridement and antibiotics. 32. Yaws is a chronic bacterial infection caused by Treponema pallidum pertenue, presenting with skin lesions and, in advanced stages, bone and soft tissue involvement.
